data.name: Lacy
data.gender_notes: Lacy is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the English word ‘lace’, this name reflects the idea of something delicate, fine, and beautiful. In the Middle Ages, lacy garments were symbols of high social status and elegance, and the name Lacy came to be associated with refined and graceful women. The name Lacy carries the meaning “Lace, delicate” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lacy usually hope their child will grow to embody lace, delicate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Lacy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lace, delicate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lacy total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lacy has historical roots in England during the Middle Ages. At that time, lace was an expensive and intricate textile, often made by hand. Wearing clothing adorned with lace was a sign of wealth and social standing. As the name Lacy became associated with the history of lace, it came to symbolize refinement, grace, and elegance.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Lacy can be interpreted as a reminder of the delicate nature of human life. Lacy can inspire us to treat every moment and every interaction with care, as if it were a precious and unique work of art. Additionally, the name Lacy can serve as a reminder of the refined and beautiful qualities of the divine. In Christian tradition, God is often described as the Master Craftsman who intricately designs and cares for each individual soul. As bears of God's image, we too are called to be creative andornamental in our lives, reflecting the beauty and grace of the divine.
